chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Hallal said: Yasir said from one of the slaves from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) that he said:
The servant continues to steal until, when he has fully paid the price of his hand, Allah exposes it against him.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of habitual stealing has on a person according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) elucidates the concept of *tadarruj* (gradual progression) in sin, where habitual theft hardens the heart until the divine penalty for the 'hand'—whether physical amputation or spiritual exposure—is fully incurred. It highlights the Shia scholarly understanding that the 'price' of the hand is not merely the act itself but the cumulative spiritual debt that Allah eventually reveals, serving as a warning against the normalization of minor sins.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ahmad Bin Umar Al Hallal, from Yasir, from one of the slaves, 
From Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘If a servant does not stop from stealing even after he is satisfied with his wages, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Exposes it against him’.
